piece: W1-15 round 4 critic — interior lighting, stealth, fencing, crime
next_step: none — verdict, ledger, publish and blog line are landed. The one open re-measurement is named in the verdict: retake the LIT_CAP frame time on an idle box with a real GPU context.
findings: THIRD LIGHTING SITE, unclaimed: engine.js#cellFor() routes writ-house and barge-hold to render/places.js, which builds its own PointLights and never calls world/interior-lighting.js. writ-house: 47 of 108 floor cells drawn lit and simulated dark (43.5%) — the round-3 defect verbatim, in the game's second room. barge-hold: 2 drawn vs 3 simulated, brightest sources 3.8 m apart. 1 of the round's own eleven fail-open rooms (writ-house) does NOT get the shared fail-open.

k RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY AND CORRECT: max aperture ratio 0.102565 (blackrose-house-1, 12.94x4.34 m, 8 panes), k=2.5350; declared bounds give 8.0600; 112 of 115 shrunk; archon-apothecary 13.60x15.60 -> 9.83x4.98. Exact.

SATURATION: 12,210 of 16,996 indoor floor cells (71.8%) sit at L=1.0000 at noon clear; 10 rooms entirely flat. Round 3 was 69.4% / 7 flat. Pre-existing property of authored_intensity_to_L_scale, but the round published it at ROOM granularity (11 rooms) and not at CELL granularity.

VACUITY GUARD CANNOT GO RED: staged a copy where syncCoverVolumes() still exists, is still called in the fixed step, and returns an empty list. All six VACUITY rows still PASS and the tool exits 0. The guard tests for an ABSENT NAME, never for an INERT PRODUCER.

RULE-6 SHAPE LABELS INVERTED against rule 6's own text: on the disagreement measurement only site A bites (0->1215; B is 0->0), which is ONE site; on the eleven-rooms measurement BOTH bite alone (0.1676->0.1102 and ->0.0974), which is two INDEPENDENT sites, not "two guards for one defect" (rule 6: "deleting either alone changes nothing").

FOURTH RAW-TOTAL CONSUMER: disposition.js:313 `-G.fDispCrimeMod * player.bounty` where _questPlayerView() (engine.js:9074) sums ALL bounty jurisdictions with no unattributed subtraction. fDispCrimeMod=0.02, so the round's own 680 g unattributed scenario costs -13.6 disposition with every person in the province.

VERIFIED: 0 disagreeing cells of 16,996 on an instrument this critic wrote; renderer-side cut (which the round's 2x2 never ran) bites — 706->500 point lights, 0->94 cells; fence 1,787/1,787 refusable with control 0, and 5-8 of 9 fences still buy so the economy has an out.
CANOPY_DAY clamp is unreachable by construction (0 rooms), so interiorAmbientL().clamped can never be true on the shipped corpus.

FRAME TIME, the round's own unmeasured reversal condition: thorn-hall through the shipped render path, 5 point lights median 3,240.9 ms vs 14 point lights median 10,813.8 ms (n=40 each) = 3.34x. As worded the reversal condition is MET. NOT reversing the ruling on it: 4-7 browser instances and 5.0-7.5 load per core throughout, a 3.2 s frame at five lights is not a GPU, my probe failed to identify the rasteriser, and the 40-lamp control did not finish. Named the re-measurement that would settle it.
could_not_do: The live third-site arm never ran — the probe was cut at its timeout after two of four frame-time arms. §1's writ-house and barge-hold findings are OFFLINE, from the real render/places.js and the real litLights(), not from a live walk. The verdict's provenance line says so.
The 40-lamp control arm (the check that the frame-time instrument can see lamp cost at all) did not complete at load 5-7.5/core. The instrument's credibility rests on the weaker 5->14 monotone step.
tools/run-all.mjs and the 29-assertion stl-live.mjs — both launch many browsers; the box was over its instance ceiling for most of the run.
RI-QST05 was not re-measured; its 3 is inherited from round 3 and is the weakest number in the score table. RI-CRM02 rests on one spot-check (crime.writs has no producer in game/src).
The round's predecessor's two open probes (a live loadState round trip and a live answerArrest('pay')) are STILL OPEN, open since round 2, and I did not attempt them either.

My own instrument has a defect I am recording rather than hiding: the WEBGL_debug_renderer_info probe reported `none` because E.renderer.renderer is not the WebGLRenderer on this build, so I cannot say which rasteriser produced the frame times.

COMMIT MESSAGE / CONTENT MISMATCH, recorded rather than rewritten: commit 64a4b01's message says the frame-time retry was 'still running', but the verdict file that commit carries already contains §10.5 with the numbers. The index was locked by two concurrent banks for ~20 minutes and the retry loop landed after the message was written. Correcting the record here rather than rewriting a shared tree.

node tools/publish.mjs exits 1, on a NEIGHBOUR's verdict: 'w1-attr-scale-r1 plots on no chart because its piece id maps to no domain'. w1-15 is in tools/scores.mjs's DOMAIN at line 50 and this verdict charts. Pre-existing and not mine; recorded because a non-zero publish is worth someone's minute.
note_on_shared_paths: reports/blog-feed.jsonl and docs/shots/ are appended by every finishing piece; ownership --conflicts reports them against AUDIT-R1-LIST, P10-loader-retry and PLAYABILITY. One appended line and one new dated filename each — declared rather than left to read as a collision.
